ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: The first great steppe empire of eastern Eurasia, united by Modu Chanyu around 209 BCE, forced Han China into decades of appeasement.
The 'peace through kinship' arrangement of annual gifts and Han brides that bought peace from the Xiongnu after the Battle of Baideng.
Founded by Bumin in 552, the first state to bear the name Türk managed Silk Road commerce and left the Orkhon Inscriptions.
A western steppe power poised between Byzantium and the caliphate, notable for its religious pluralism and its rulers' conversion to Judaism.
Temüjin unified the rival Mongol and Turkic tribes and was proclaimed Genghis Khan at a kurultai in 1206.
Decimal units, promotion by merit and the yam relay system carried Mongol armies from China to Legnica and Mohi by 1241.
The body of Mongol customary law that Genghis Khan's heirs, Chagatai above all, enforced across the conquered lands.
The Central Asian appanage of Genghis Khan's second son shows the lasting tension between nomadic tradition and the sedentary Silk Road cities.
Rising within the Chagatai Khanate, Timur used the Mongol framework of legitimacy to build an empire from Anatolia to the borders of China.
